children.translated_text: This <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecratory rite), intended for all pregnancies, is performed only once, by way of consecrating the receptacle.
In the case of another wife, however, it must indeed be performed during her first pregnancy.

children.text: darśādūrdhvam ā darśādeko māsaḥ yatra kvaca dine'pyāhite garbhe sa eko māso gaṇayitavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From one new-moon day until the next new-moon day is one month. If pregnancy was established on any day within that interval, that entire interval is to be counted as one month.
The designation is for the sake of practical usage.

children.text: atra kecit atikrānte'pi mukhyakāle prasavāt prākkālātikramaprāyaścittaṃ kṛtvā kartavyamevetyāhuḥ upanayane darśanāt tena ca smṛtiṣu tulyavadgaṇanāt kāsucit smṛtiṣu kālānirdeśena vidhānād āpatkalpatayābhyanujñānaṃ sarvadā saṃskārāṇām astyevetyāhuḥ jananādūrdhvaṃ tu dvārābhāvāt prāyaścittenaiva jātaṃ saṃskuryādekadeśe'gnau ||
children.translated_text: On this point, some say that even when the principal time has passed, the rite must still be performed before delivery, after carrying out the expiation for having exceeded the proper time. This follows because such a procedure is seen in the case of initiation, because this rite and initiation are reckoned alike in the <s>smṛti</s> texts, and because certain <s>smṛti</s> texts prescribe it without specifying a time. They say that permission to perform <s>saṃskāras</s> as an emergency alternative always exists. After birth, however, since the means for the rite no longer exists, one should consecrate the newborn by expiation alone—at one part, in the fire.

children.text: garbhāntarārthaṃ tu dvitīye garbhe kuryād eva ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of a subsequent pregnancy, however, one should certainly perform it during the second pregnancy.
Others say that when the proper time has passed, there is no longer eligibility and only expiation should be performed.
The former position, however, is preferable.

children.text: athāpi lopasaṃśaye lopād alopo nyāyataraḥ iti nidānakāro'pyāha ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, even when there is doubt whether an omission has occurred, non-omission is more reasonable than omission; so too says the author of the <s>Nidāna</s>.
With a new lower garment and a new upper garment.

children.text: brahmopaveśanāntaṃ kṛtvā vadhūṃ dakṣiṇato darbheṣūpaveśya prapadāntaṃ kṛtvānvārabdhāyāṃ vyāhṛtibhis tisṛbhir ājyaṃ hutvā punaśca hutvā vadhvāḥ paścāddarbheṣu tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the ritual through the seating of the <s>brahman</s>, he should seat the bride on <s>darbha</s> grass to the south. Having performed it through the stage called <s>prapadānta</s>, while she is touching him, he should offer ghee with the three <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, make another offering, and then stand on <s>darbha</s> grass behind the bride.
The word “husband” is used to prescribe the authorized guardian in the husband's absence.

children.text: bharturanyaḥ kurvan praṇīte laukike vā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If someone other than the husband performs the rite, he should do so in a specially brought fire or in an ordinary domestic fire.
